question: Does my state tax my pension or my Social Security?

nuggets.text: Social Security benefits are subtracted from Virginia taxable income.
nuggets.quote: Benefits received under Title II of the Social Security Act and other benefits subject to federal income taxation solely pursuant to § 86 of the Internal Revenue Code.

nuggets.text: Pensions are taxed, with an age deduction of up to $12,000 at 65 or older.
nuggets.quote: A deduction in the amount of $ 12,000 for individuals born after January 1, 1939, who have attained the age of 65.

nuggets.text: The age deduction is reduced as income rises above $50,000 or $75,000.
nuggets.quote: This deduction shall be reduced by $ 1 for every $ 1 that the taxpayer's adjusted federal adjusted gross income exceeds $ 50,000 for single taxpayers or $ 75,000 for married taxpayers.

nuggets.text: Up to $40,000 of military benefits may be subtracted from 2025.
nuggets.quote: for taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2025, up to $40,000 of military benefits.
